name: Isotropic Total Variation
definition: A regularization prior that sums the magnitude of the gradient at each voxel. It is defined using a forward difference matrix $D$ and a matrix $E$ denoting positions of forward differences, expressed as the norm $\|\mathbf{q}\|_E$ for $\mathbf{q} = D\mathbf{f}$.
summary: Isotropic Total Variation is a volumetric regularization that uses the Euclidean norm of gradient vectors to prevent directional bias and produce smoother, more natural edges than anisotropic methods.
